mainTopic: Does a married woman's acquisition automatically go to her husband (יד אשה כיד בעלה)? רב's ruling is tied to רבי מאיר, challenged from the rules of שיתופי מבואות, and answered by רבא.
overview: The גמרא asks which תנא רב's ruling follows. רב's ruling is that whatever a married woman acquires goes to her husband. The answer is רבי מאיר, who said that 'the hand of a woman is like the hand of her husband.' A משנה about merging an alleyway (שיתוף מבואות) seems to contradict this. It says a man may give the shared food to the residents through his wife, but if her hand is his hand, the food never leaves him. רבא answers that רבי מאיר agrees she can acquire from her husband when she does it for others. רבינא challenges this with a ברייתא that puts the wife on the list of people who cannot acquire for others. So רב אשי gives a new answer: the משנה is about a wife who owns her own courtyard in that alley, and since she acquires for herself, she acquires for the others too. Then a new משנה begins. A widow or divorcée who vowed to be a נזירה starting in thirty days, and married within that time, keeps her vow, because her new husband cannot annul it.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רב's ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view רב's ruling matches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ruling of רב follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which earlier sage (תנא) agrees with רב's ruling that what a married woman acquires belongs to her husband. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling is not obvious, because normally a person can acquire things for himself. So the גמרא looks for a תנא whose principle could support it. Finding that source will also expose it to challenges.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does it follow?
A teaching or ruling (here, רב's ruling)
The early אמורא whose ruling is being discussed

phrases.english: In accordance with whom does this ruling of Rav go?
phrases.notes: This is רב's ruling that what a married woman acquires goes to her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line of inquiry about רב's ruling from earlier in the sugya.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion supports רב's ruling that a wife's acquisition goes to her husband.

steps.title: רב follows רבי מאיר: a wife's hand is like her husband's
steps.stepSummary: רב's ruling matches רבי מאיר, who says a woman's hand is like her husband's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי מאיר, who said: the hand of a woman is like the hand of her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's ruling fits רבי מאיר's principle: whatever comes into a wife's hand is treated as if it came into her husband's hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גמרא's words, רבי מאיר himself said that a woman's hand is like her husband's hand. רבא repeats this in step 5. On this view, whatever a married woman acquires automatically becomes her husband's, and that is exactly רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose principle is used to support רב
A wife's hand is like her husband's hand: what she acquires, he acquires

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is what the rest of the sugya tests. The challenge in the next steps attacks this very idea.

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi Meir, who said:
The hand of a woman is like the hand of her husband.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב follows רבי מאיר's principle that a wife's hand is like her husband's hand.

steps.title: A משנה: a man may merge the alley through his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that lets a man transfer the shared alley food to the residents through his wife, among others.
steps.simpleTranslation: And raise a contradiction: How does one merge an alleyway? He places a barrel and says, 'This is for all the residents of the alley.' He gives them ownership through his Hebrew slave or maidservant, through his adult son or daughter, and through his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that seems to clash with רבי מאיר's principle. This step only quotes the source; the actual problem comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To merge an alleyway (שיתוף), the food must truly belong to all the residents. So someone has to accept it on their behalf. The משנה lists people who are not part of the giver himself, and that list includes his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: a source is set against the previous claim
Merging an alleyway (שיתוף מבואות) so people may carry there on שבת
Transfers ownership to others through someone acting for them
A Jewish (Hebrew) slave, who is not his master's property

steps.confusionAlert: The person accepting the food must count as separate from the giver. Otherwise the food never really leaves the giver's possession. Keep this in mind for the next step.

phrases.english: And raise a contradiction: How does one merge an alleyway?
He places the barrel and says:
This is for all the residents of the alleyway.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְזַכֶּה לָהֶן עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִים,
phrases.english: And he transfers ownership to them through his Hebrew slave and maidservant,
and through his adult son and daughter,
and through his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge the principle given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's principle יד אשה כיד בעלה as the basis for רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the משנה lets a wife receive the food for others, which will be shown to clash with the principle.

steps.title: If her hand is his, the food never left him
steps.stepSummary: If the husband acquires whatever his wife receives, then giving the food through her would accomplish nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say her husband acquires them, then the עירוב food never left the husband's possession!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the problem clearly. If the wife's hand is the husband's hand, then handing her the food is like handing it to himself, so the alley residents never get it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says giving through a wife works. רבי מאיר's principle says she cannot acquire apart from her husband. Both cannot be true unless something explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: introduces the problem with your claim
The shared food that allows carrying on שבת
Domain or possession

phrases.english: And if you say her husband acquires them,
the eiruv has not left the husband's domain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the contradiction from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle יד אשה כיד בעלה (and so רב's ruling).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wife's acquisition goes to her husband, the food never leaves him, so the שיתוף could not work. Yet the משנה says it works.

steps.title: רבא: acquiring for others is different
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי מאיר agrees about שיתוף. Since the wife takes the food only to acquire it for others, she can acquire it from her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even though רבי מאיר said a woman's hand is like her husband's hand, he agrees regarding שיתוף. Since she is acquiring it for others from her husband, she does acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction. He keeps רבי מאיר's principle but says it does not block her from acquiring for other people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle only means that what she gets for herself goes to her husband. Here she is not acquiring for herself. She is acting for the alley residents, so she can take it from her husband on their behalf. רב's ruling still stands in normal cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who answers the challenge
Even though
Agrees (concedes in this case)
To acquire on behalf of others
She acquires

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first answer: רבי מאיר's principle covers what she acquires for herself, not what she takes from her husband for others. Watch for step 7, where רב אשי drops this answer and gives a different one.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not reject the principle. It still applies when she acquires for herself. The exception is only for acquiring on behalf of others.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Meir said
the hand of a woman is like the hand of her husband,
Rabbi Meir agrees regarding merging,
that since it is to acquire for others
from her husband's hand, she acquires.
phrases.notes: She takes the food from her husband not for herself but for the alley residents, so it truly leaves his possession.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the principle: it applies when she acquires for herself, but not when she acquires for others.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought יד אשה כיד בעלה means she can never acquire anything apart from her husband, which would make the משנה's שיתוף impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר agrees that a wife can acquire from her husband on behalf of others, so the שיתוף works and רב's ruling is not contradicted.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a wife cannot acquire for others
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רב אשי with a ברייתא that lists a wife among those who cannot acquire the עירוב food for others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged רב אשי: These are the people through whom one can acquire for others: his adult son and daughter, and his Hebrew slave and maidservant. And these are the people through whom one cannot acquire for others: his minor son and daughter, his Canaanite slave and maidservant, and his wife!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא quotes a ברייתא that clearly says a man cannot transfer the עירוב food to others through his wife. This attacks the answer from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said a wife can acquire the שיתוף for others, because she is only acting for them. This ברייתא puts the wife on the 'cannot' list, next to minors and Canaanite slaves. That suggests her hand counts as her husband's hand even when she acts for others.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
They acquire for them (on behalf of others)
Hebrew slave, who keeps his own independent status
Canaanite slave, whose hand is like his master's hand
Minors, who cannot legally acquire for others

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection to Rav Ashi:
These are the ones through whom one acquires for others:
through his adult son and daughter,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets; the meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: and his Hebrew slave and maidservant.
And these are the ones through whom one cannot acquire for others:
through his minor son and daughter,
and his Canaanite slave and maidservant, and his wife!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 5 that a wife can acquire the שיתוף for others.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer that a wife can acquire for others from her husband when she acts on their behalf. The ברייתא also clashes with the משנה in step 3, which lists the wife as able to acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly lists the wife among those who cannot acquire the עירוב for others. So the answer cannot be right.

steps.title: The wife owns her own courtyard in the alley
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי drops the earlier answer. He explains that the משנה is talking about a wife who owns her own courtyard in that alley, so she acquires for herself and therefore for others too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Our משנה is dealing with a case where she has a courtyard of her own in that alley. Since she acquires for herself, she also acquires for others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new answer to the original question from steps 3 and 4. It replaces רבא's answer from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier answer is dropped. In general a wife's hand is like her husband's hand, as the ברייתא says. But here she owns her own courtyard in the alley, so she is one of the residents herself. Because she acquires her own share, she can acquire the shares of the others as well (מגו).

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals the earlier answer is dropped)
Courtyard
Alleyway shared by several courtyards
Since (since she can do X, she can also do Y)
We are dealing with

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean every wife can acquire for others. It only works because this wife owns her own courtyard in that alley, so she is herself one of the residents.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife normally cannot acquire the עירוב for others through her husband. The משנה allowing it is about a wife who owns her own courtyard in the alley.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Our mishnah is where she has a courtyard
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in עירובין quoted in step 3.

phrases.english: in that alley, we are dealing with;
for since she acquires for herself,
she acquires for others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 6 and replaces step 5's answer with a new explanation of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about a wife who owns her own courtyard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wife can acquire for others from her husband whenever she acts on their behalf.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wife can acquire for others only when she owns a courtyard in that alley. Since she acquires for herself, she also acquires for others.

steps.title: New משנה: the vow of a widow or divorcée stands
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the פסוק that an אלמנה's or גרושה's vow stands: if she vowed נזירות to start in thirty days and married before then, her new husband cannot annul it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: "But the vow of a widow or a divorcée shall stand against her." How so? If she said, "I am hereby a נזירה after thirty days," then even if she married within those thirty days, her husband cannot annul it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and explains a פסוק about the vows of a widow or divorcée. It gives a case where the vow was made before marriage but only takes effect after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow was made while she was not married to anyone. So even though the נזירות only begins after she marries, the new husband has no power to cancel it. What counts is when she made the vow, not when it takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Widow
Divorced woman
Shall stand against her (remains binding)
A woman who takes a nazirite vow
To annul (a vow)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a husband's power to annul applies only to vows made while she is under his authority, even if the vow takes effect later.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: "But the vow of a widow and a divorcée
shall stand against her." How so?
If she said: "I am hereby a nazirite
after thirty days,"

he cannot annul.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְנֵדֶר אַלְמָנָה וּגְרוּשָׁהּ יָקוּם עָלֶיהָ כֵּיצַד

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow made by a widow or divorcée before marriage cannot be annulled by her new husband, even if it takes effect after the marriage.
